is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

recently_moved_to_uk.description: Whether the claimant has recently moved to the UK.

right_to_reside_status.description: A plain English description of the claimant's right-to-reside position.

Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions. Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes, I'm asking about my son Alex. He's 8 years old and lives with me at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you're inquiring about your son Alex, who is 8 years old and lives with you.

Now I need to ask you a few more questions to assess your eligibility:

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK. Though I should mention - I've only recently moved here, so I'm not entirely sure about all the requirements yet.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know. Since you've recently moved to the UK, I need to ask some additional questions about your immigration status and right to reside, as this affects eligibility.

**What is your immigration status in the UK? For example, do you have:**
- British citizenship
- Settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme
- Pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme
- Indefinite leave to remain
- Or another type of visa or status?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not really sure about the technical details of my status. I know I'm allowed to be here, but I haven't fully sorted out all the paperwork and documentation yet. It's all a bit unclear to me at the moment, to be honest.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand - immigration status can be quite complex and confusing.

Unfortunately, to properly assess your eligibility for Child Benefit, your immigration status and right to reside in the UK are critical factors. The rules vary significantly depending on whether you have:
- Settled status
- Pre-settled status (which has additional conditions like working or having sufficient resources)
- Other types of leave to remain
- Or if you're still in the process of establishing your status

**Do you have any documentation at all that might indicate your status - such as:**
- A biometric residence permit card
- An EU Settlement Scheme status confirmation
- A visa in your passport
- Any letters from the Home Office

**Or, alternatively, are you currently in the process of applying for a particular immigration status?**

This information is essential because different statuses have different Child Benefit eligibility rules attached to them.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I do have some documentation, but honestly I'm not entirely clear on what it all means or what my exact status is. I came here recently and I'm still trying to understand the UK system. I know I'm here legally, but the specifics of my right to reside status - I just don't have a clear answer for you on that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I completely understand - navigating the UK immigration system can be very complex, especially when you've recently arrived.

The challenge is that Child Benefit eligibility depends heavily on having a clear understanding of your right to reside in the UK. Different types of status have very different rules attached to them. For example:

- Some statuses allow you to claim Child Benefit immediately
- Others require you to be working and earning above a certain threshold
- Some have restrictions if you're claiming certain other benefits

**Since you're uncertain about your exact immigration status and right to reside, I have a couple of suggestions:**

1. **Would you be able to check your documentation and find out what your specific status is?** This might be on a card, letter, or digital confirmation from the Home Office or EU Settlement Scheme.

2. **Or, would you prefer I make an assessment based on the information I do have?** In that case, I would need to report that your eligibility is **indeterminate** because without knowing your immigration status and right to reside, I cannot definitively say whether you meet the Child Benefit eligibility requirements.

Which would you prefer?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I understand it's important, but honestly I've looked at my papers and I still can't give you a clear answer about my exact status. I think it's best if you just assess based on what you know - that I'm here in the UK legally with Alex, but my right to reside situation isn't clear. If that means you can't give me a definite answer, I understand.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for being so clear about your situation. I appreciate your honesty.

Based on what you've told me, let me summarize:

- You have an 8-year-old son, Alex, who lives with you
- You both live in the UK
- You are here legally, but the specifics of your immigration status and right to reside are unclear

Before I make my final assessment, I need to ask one more important question about Alex:

**Is Alex in any special circumstances, such as:**
- Being in hospital or residential care for an extended period
- Living with someone else for part of the time
- Working 24 hours or more per week
- Claiming benefits in his own right

Or is he simply living at home with you full-time as a typical 8-year-old?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nothing like that. He's just a typical 8-year-old living at home with me full-time. He goes to school and comes home - just normal family life.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:

- ✓ He's 8 years old (under 16)

- ✓ He's not in any special circumstances that would affect eligibility

3. **You may still want to apply** - Even though I cannot confirm eligibility, you could submit an application and let HMRC make the official determination based on your documentation.
